text:
sam: Quick question about the /embeddings endpoint — want to confirm contract details before I send a client PR. TL;DR: allowed input types, where truncation happens, batch limits, and how output vectors map to inputs.

leila: Go ahead — hit the specifics you need.

sam: 1) Can we accept a mix of strings and nulls in the same array? 2) Is truncation applied per-item or across the whole request? 3) What's the default max items per request (and is that configurable per customer)? 4) Output shape: do we guarantee 1:1 ordering (i.e., output[i] corresponds to input[i]) and what do we return for null/empty inputs?

jia: Short answers: 1) yes, we accept mixed types but we prefer explicit nulls for empty entries; 2) truncation is per-item (we run tokenizer on each string independently); 3) default item cap is 512 per request (can be raised for Dedicated customers); 4) yes, ordering is preserved. For null/empty entries we return an empty vector placeholder (zero-length) plus a corresponding metadata entry with reason.

ben: Adding nuance: when a string exceeds per-item token limit it gets truncated to model max_length, not the batch combined length. We also attach a "truncated": true flag in the per-item meta. Example returned item meta in current API: 
```
{"index": 3, "truncated": true, "original_tokens": 12000, "kept_tokens": 8192}
```

marta: On the zero-length placeholder — client teams asked whether we return null vs [] vs a vector of zeros. Current decision: return null for embeddings + add a top-level errors array for items with no embedding. Rationale: avoids misleading cosine-similarity with zero-vectors. We also emit a warning log and a metric (embeddings.empty_input.count).

sam: Good. For the PR I need the exact response shape example so SDKs can deserialize properly. Can we get one canonical success + partial-truncation + empty example?

jia: Sure, here's the current canonical shape (stringified for the thread):
```
{
  "data": [
    {"input_index": 0, "embedding": [0.001, -0.23, ...], "dimensions": 1536, "meta": {"truncated": false}},
    {"input_index": 1, "embedding": null, "dimensions": 0, "meta": {"truncated": false, "reason": "empty_input"}},
    {"input_index": 2, "embedding": [0.12, 0.05, ...], "dimensions": 1536, "meta": {"truncated": true, "original_tokens": 10000, "kept_tokens": 8192}}
  ],
  "model": "open-embed-large-v2",
  "usage": {"items": 3, "tokens": 16432},
  "warnings": ["1 item truncated"],
  "errors": [ {"index": 1, "code": "EMPTY_INPUT", "message": "empty input, no embedding returned"} ]
}
```

leila: That matches what we've been shipping in prod for a month. One small change: the embedding vectors are floats serialized as arrays; we don't pad null embeddings with zeros anywhere. SDKs should treat embedding null as a separate code path.

ben: Also note that streaming mode for embeddings (experimental) yields the same contract but sends per-item records over the stream. Ordering is preserved.

sam: Thanks — regarding batching, what's the behavior if a request has ~600 small strings (all under token limit) and default cap is 512? Do we return 429 or auto-split and process multiple batches?

jia: Current behavior: we enforce the item cap at the API gateway. If items > cap we return 400 with error code TOO_MANY_ITEMS and include a suggested split size. For Dedicated customers we offer a soft quota bump (proxy-side) and we can auto-split inside the runtime for specific SDKs, but the public API doesn't auto-split to avoid hidden billing surprises.

marta: Operational note: if you want auto-splitting in SDKs we recommend adding an opt-in flag so callers know they're being billed for multiple requests implicitly.

sam: Good call. For backward-compat — any fields we might remove soon? I want to avoid landing-breaking changes in the SDK PR.

leila: No removals planned. We might add a new per-item score field later (confidence), but it'll be optional and nullable. Always prefer additive changes.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline notice: embedding-service v3.14 rolled out to canary at 2001234580. No errors seen in initial telemetry.

ben: One more thing — character encoding: we normalize inputs to NFC and then run tokenizer. Clients don't need to normalize, but tests should include combining characters to verify consistency.

sam: Perfect. I'll draft the client PR with these contract examples and mark the tests. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

leila: Ping if you want a quick review of the test cases.

sam: Will do.
